## Atacama's Moon Valley: walking among salt, sand and rock

[Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) lies in the Cordillera de la Sal, near [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The area is unlike familiar desert landscapes: salt ridges, dunes, exposed rock layers and deep furrows stand side by side. Wind and water shaped the surface over a long period, and the contrast between sunlit and shaded slopes makes the valley especially striking in the evening.

The Ada Tours excursion takes place **in the afternoon** and ends with **sunset viewing from a lookout**, followed by a return to the hotel. Departure time, the length of the walk and any paid extras are confirmed for the specific program.

## Why the valley has a "lunar" landscape

The name Valle de la Luna reflects the unusual appearance of this treeless area. Pale salt formations alternate with reddish and ochre-colored rock. Erosion has produced forms resembling towers, waves and long stone ridges.

The valley is an interesting place to compare different surfaces. The salt crust looks light and sometimes crystalline, sandy slopes are smoother, and exposed rock records the effects of weathering. It is the combination of these features, rather than a single stone monument, that creates the impression of an otherworldly landscape.

Moon Valley is part of the **Los Flamencos National Reserve**. Its protected status means visitors must use authorized paths and follow access rules. Fragile salt formations are easily damaged, so do not leave official trails just to take photographs.

## Why excursions are scheduled toward evening

The sun's angle changes throughout the day. In the evening, long shadows emphasize the ridges and folds of the land. At sunset the rocks can take on **red, orange and purple shades**.

The intensity of the colors depends on cloud cover, air clarity and the chosen viewpoint. This is natural light: a particular palette or a completely cloudless sky cannot be guaranteed.

For photography, charge your phone or camera beforehand and avoid spending all your time on a single view. The journey and walking section offer different subjects: wide desert panoramas, salt textures, curved dunes and sunlit ledges.

## What to bring on the walk

The Atacama is known for dry air and substantial temperature changes. It can cool quickly after sunset. Closed, non-slip shoes, a hat, water, sunglasses and an extra evening jacket are useful.

Some sections may be dusty or windy. Consider the altitude, ground conditions and actual walking duration, especially if the excursion follows several active days on the Altiplano.

This is **a landscape walk**, not a sporting climb, salt-mine visit or an overnight telescope experience. Ada Tours offers a separate [Atacama astronomy excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/chile-atacama-astronomy-tour/) for exploring the night sky.

## Combining Moon Valley with other days in Chile

The visit fits well into an itinerary based in San Pedro. Daytime can be used for other excursions, with the evening devoted to rock formations and sunset light. When planning a [Chile journey](/chile/tour/), allow for travel distances to high-altitude lagoons and geysers: these belong to other excursions with their own conditions.

The price and included services for this standalone excursion have not yet been specified. Confirm the details for the selected departure rather than automatically borrowing transfers and meals from other Atacama programs.

## Frequently asked questions about Moon Valley

### Where is Moon Valley?

In the **Cordillera de la Sal** near San Pedro de Atacama, within Los Flamencos National Reserve.

### When does the walk take place?

The published itinerary schedules **the afternoon** and sunset viewing, followed by a return to the hotel. Exact times depend on the departure.

### Will the rocks turn purple every evening?

Their colors depend on cloud cover and light. Sunset is part of the route, but a particular landscape color is not guaranteed.

### Is this the same as an astronomy tour?

No. Here the focus is on **landforms and evening light**, whereas the astronomy excursion focuses on the night sky and telescopes.

## Tours featuring Atacama's Moon Valley: a walk and desert sunset

[Atacama's Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) lies near San Pedro de Atacama, among the dry ridges of the Cordillera de la Sal. It is one of Chile's landscapes where sand dunes and salt formations change most dramatically in evening light. The [Atacama Moon Valley: Walk and Sunset excursion](/chile/moon-valley-atacama/atacama-moon-valley-sunset-walk/) focuses on exploring the valley on foot and watching sunset from a viewpoint.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring this specific standalone excursion. The linked journeys include [Hidden Treasures of Chile: Atacama, Patagonia and the Marble Caves](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) and [Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile: 16 Days from Uyuni to Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). In the first, travelers fly to the Atacama from Santiago; in the second, they enter the Chilean desert after crossing Bolivia's highlands.

## When the excursion takes place on each tour

| Route | Moon Valley visit |
|---|---|
| [Chile, 9 days](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) | Day 2, after arriving in Calama |
| [Bolivia and Chile, 16 days](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) | Day 5, after El Tatio geysers |

On **the nine-day Chile itinerary**, travelers fly from Santiago to Calama on day two and then transfer to San Pedro de Atacama. Moon Valley and sunset viewing are scheduled for the afternoon. On this particular tour, **admission and a cocktail are included**. After the desert, the program continues to high-altitude lagoons, salt flats and geysers, then to southern Chile, including Patagonia and the Marble Caves.

On **the sixteen-day Bolivia and Chile journey**, Moon Valley is scheduled for day five. Travelers visit El Tatio geysers in the morning, have breakfast and visit thermal springs. After returning and resting, they set out for the sunset excursion. By then, they have seen the Uyuni Salt Flat and Bolivia's lagoons; Santiago and Patagonia lie ahead. Moon Valley becomes a transition between high-altitude landscapes and another side of Chilean nature.

These two programs differ in more than their total durations. On one, the Atacama is an introduction to Chile after Santiago; on the other, it continues a journey through Bolivia's deserts and salt flats. If you want to see the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), choose an itinerary that actually includes it rather than assuming any Chile tour can be extended to do so.

## What you will see on the walk

The attraction lies within **Los Flamencos National Reserve**. You will encounter salt ridges, dunes and rock formations shaped by natural erosion. In the evening their colors can shift from reddish to purple. How they appear depends on weather and light, so a specific sunset color cannot be guaranteed.

The excursion is a walk through the desert landscape, followed by sunset at a viewpoint and return to the accommodation. It is **not a nighttime astronomy tour** or a geyser excursion; other itinerary sections cover those experiences. The duration of the walk, transport services and standalone excursion price are agreed separately. Admission and a cocktail are specifically confirmed only for the nine-day tour and must not be assumed to be included on every journey.

## Preparing for the sunset visit

Strong daytime sunshine in the Atacama can be followed by a noticeable temperature drop after sunset. Bring comfortable closed shoes, water, sun protection and an extra warm layer. The altitude and dry air should also influence your pace and comfort.

Departure time needs particular care when the sunset visit falls on a flight day or follows an early geyser departure. On the [nine-day tour](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/), Moon Valley comes after arriving in Calama; on the [sixteen-day tour](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/), it finishes the day after El Tatio. Do not add more long-distance trips that evening without considering travel time and logistics.

## Frequently asked questions about tours with Moon Valley

### Which tours already feature this excursion?

Both [the nine-day Hidden Treasures of Chile](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) and [the sixteen-day Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) explicitly link to this excursion module.

### Which day includes the sunset walk?

Day two of the nine-day Chile itinerary and day five of the journey through Bolivia.

### Is admission included?

**The nine-day tour** includes admission and a cocktail. Neither the standalone excursion nor the other tour establishes that these same services are universally included.

### Can the walk be combined with El Tatio geysers?

The sixteen-day itinerary combines them: guests visit the geysers in the morning, return to the hotel, and head to Moon Valley in the afternoon.

### What matters most when choosing between the tours?

If you primarily want to see more regions of Chile, the nine-day program is suitable. If you also want the Bolivian salt flats and the Atacama, consider the sixteen-day journey.

## Atacama Moon Valley excursion: a desert walk and sunset

[Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) (Valle de la Luna) lies near [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), amid dunes, salt ridges and dry rock formations. It is fascinating to watch the desert change color in the evening as sunlight, clouds and dust affect the shades of sand and stone.

We offer the [Atacama Moon Valley: Walk and Sunset excursion](/chile/moon-valley-atacama/atacama-moon-valley-sunset-walk/) to explore the area. Its purpose is an afternoon visit, a walk through the valley's landscapes and sunset viewing from a lookout. It is not the same as a high-altitude trip to lagoons or geysers.

## What you can see on the excursion

### Salt formations and reddish ridges

The valley belongs to the Cordillera de la Sal sector of Los Flamencos National Reserve. Sandy surfaces, salt layers and rocky outcrops form unusual combinations. The view can change dramatically within a small area, with gentle dune curves alongside sharp dry ridges.

Stay on authorized paths. Beyond them lie fragile soils and salt structures that can easily be damaged. Some sectors close because of wind, rain or the risk of falling rocks.

### Sunset as a separate part of the itinerary

Our excursion includes sunset viewing from a lookout. Shadows change on the slopes as the ridges become more defined. Yet colors do not appear to a precise timetable: the light depends on weather, air clarity and the chosen location.

Because the valley regulates visiting hours and access to individual trails, plan around the current access times rather than arriving just before the sun reaches the horizon.

## Access rules and physical demands

The reserve's official administrator, CONAF, lists designated routes in the Moon Valley sector, including **Duna Mayor**, approximately 919 m long, and **Cornisa**, approximately 718 m long. Its visitor information estimates around 45–60 minutes for each, but these are independent reserve trails. **This does not mean both trails are included in the Ada Tours excursion**: the actual itinerary is determined by the selected product.

CONAF also requires access via designated entrances and warns that entering the sector on foot from outside is not permitted: transport is required. Ticket sales, timetables, transport rules and trail availability may change. Check the rules in force with the site's operator before traveling.

The walks are relatively accessible, but heat, extremely dry air, loose ground and changes in elevation can be tiring. Closed shoes with reliable grip are preferable. Bring water, a hat, sunglasses and a light additional layer for the evening.

## Adding Moon Valley to an Atacama itinerary

Moon Valley can fit into an arrival day in the San Pedro area if flight and transfer times leave enough margin. But this cannot be promised without knowing flight schedules and local access restrictions: a short distance on a map does not remove the site's opening hours.

The [Hidden Treasures of Chile tour](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) includes Moon Valley alongside other Atacama destinations, Patagonia and the Marble Caves. Another option is [Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/), connecting the Atacama with Bolivia's high-altitude natural sites and southern Chile.

On a multi-country journey, distinguish an evening desert walk from extended travel across high mountains. [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) vary not only in the number of regions but also in time to acclimatize to altitude and weather. For nature-focused trips, browse [Chile wildlife and nature journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/chile/).

## Photographs and experiences worth looking for

Moon Valley is especially impressive in broad landscapes showing a sequence of mountain ridges and dunes. Stable footing, dust protection for cameras and awareness of wind are important. Do not climb a closed slope or cross barriers just to take a photograph.

Similar reddish desert formations exist throughout the Atacama. When comparing excursions, read the exact place name: Moon Valley is a distinct protected sector with its own routes and rules.

## Frequently asked questions about the Moon Valley excursion

### Does the excursion really take place at sunset?

The [Ada Tours itinerary](/chile/moon-valley-atacama/atacama-moon-valley-sunset-walk/) specifies an afternoon walk and sunset viewing. The exact stop sequence depends on available time and access rules.

### Can you walk into the valley from San Pedro?

CONAF rules require transport to enter the sector. Walking on the authorized trails begins inside the visiting area.

### Are special skills required?

Our excursion does not involve technical mountaineering. Closed shoes, water and consideration for heat, wind and loose ground are nevertheless important even for a short walk.

### How does Moon Valley differ from high-altitude lagoons?

It is a lower-lying desert landscape of salt ridges, dunes and sunset views. Trips to high-altitude lagoons involve different elevations, temperatures and journey times.

## Milodon Cave excursions: choosing a route from Puerto Natales

[Milodon Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/) (Cueva del Milodón) lies about 25 km north of Puerto Natales. Under its vast rock arch, remains of an extinct giant ground sloth and other material were discovered, making it an important natural and archaeological monument in Patagonia.

For travelers, choosing an excursion here is part of planning a wider route. The cave is often visited **on the way to Torres del Paine** rather than as the sole destination of an entire day. We offer several excursion programs including Milodon Cave. Their formats and inclusions differ, so the cave's name alone is not enough to make a choice.

## Which excursions include Milodon Cave?

### Standard day with lakes and Salto Grande

The [Torres del Paine: Milodon, Lakes and Salto Grande excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/) begins with a hotel departure at 07:00 and returns to Puerto Natales at around 18:45. After the cave, the route passes viewpoints of Lakes Sofía, Porteño and Toro, the Grey Lake area, Pehoé, Salto Grande waterfall, Nordenskjöld, Laguna Amarga and Mirador Sarmiento.

This is a full sightseeing option for those wanting to see several characteristic Patagonian sites in a day. The program allows time for lunch at a local restaurant, while the precise list of paid services is confirmed in the trip quotation. Do not assume every ticket and extra service is included just because the excursion lasts all day.

### Private excursion with lunch

Another option is [Torres del Paine: A Private Day with Milodon and the Lakes](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/). It also visits the cave, lakes and park viewpoints, but is explicitly designated as a private excursion. This program **includes admission fees and lunch at a local restaurant**.

The private format suits travelers who prefer an agreed pace and stops reflecting their interests. However, it does not automatically mean unlimited itinerary changes, unrestricted time or any conceivable transfer arrangements: check the exact terms of the offer.

### The cave and a boat trip to Grey Glacier

A third option is [Torres del Paine and Grey Glacier: Boat, Lakes and Milodon](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/). Its major difference is **boat navigation to Grey Glacier**. National park admission, the boat segment and lunch are included. Milodon Cave appears alongside the lakes as part of the overall route.

Choose this day if your priority is seeing the glacier from the water and the cave is an additional historical and natural stop. Weather and navigation conditions affect the boat itinerary, so its sequence and the possibility of sailing are confirmed before departure.

## What to see inside the natural monument

The main cave has an impressive wide entrance and a high vault. Fragments of milodon skin and remains were found here, as well as evidence of ancient human presence. This is a **paleontological and archaeological story**, distinct from a simple stop for mountain photographs.

According to CONAF, the natural monument includes several caves and rock shelters. A short trail to the Large Cave is approximately **350 m** long, with an official average walking time of **30 minutes**. Longer routes also exist, but their availability does not mean they are included in every Ada Tours sightseeing excursion.

CONAF publishes separate access hours, restrictions on particular sections and safety rules. In October 2026, a temporary closure of a short section inside the main cave until the end of the year was noted. This is not the same as closing the entire monument. Check the current restrictions again before traveling.

## Comparing the programs without confusion

| Format | Main difference |
|---|---|
| Standard day | Cave and many viewpoint stops |
| Private day | Private format, admission and lunch |
| With Grey Glacier | Boat section to the glacier |

Compare the itineraries by **the main purpose of your day**. If the cave and scenic lakes are your priorities, choose the standard outing. If you value the private format and confirmed inclusions, review the corresponding program. If seeing the glacier from the water matters most, choose the boat itinerary and take its weather dependency into account.

The natural monument lies in the [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) area. It also appears on longer journeys such as [Patagonian Expanse: Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chile-argentina-journey/) and [Chile and Argentina: Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/). When selecting a long itinerary, check the particular day to understand how much time remains for lakes, walks and the Argentine border.

## Preparing for a visit

Closed shoes with non-slip soles and clothing for Patagonia's changeable weather are useful at the cave. Winds and rain nearby can be strong. Even if the cave walk itself is relatively short, the complete excursion runs from early morning until evening.

Follow marked paths at the natural monument, do not collect geological or archaeological objects and obey rangers' instructions. For visitors with limited mobility, CONAF describes an accessible section with assistance leading to an interior viewing area, but the condition of the path and any current restrictions should be checked.

## Frequently asked questions about Milodon Cave excursions

### How much time does the cave itself require?

CONAF estimates around 30 minutes for the short path to the Large Cave. On a multi-stop excursion, the day's itinerary determines the time allocated.

### Is Milodon Cave inside Torres del Paine National Park?

No. It is a separate natural monument near Puerto Natales, often visited en route to the national park.

### Which excursion includes the glacier boat trip?

Choose the [Grey Glacier boat program](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/). Do not assume that navigation is included on the other listed excursions unless explicitly specified.

### What is included in the private day excursion price?

The [private excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) includes admission and lunch. Other terms depend on the offer and arrangements for the specific journey.

## Valparaíso Navy Headquarters excursions: Plaza Sotomayor and the port city

The historic [Valparaíso Navy Headquarters](/chile/place/navy-headquarters-valparaiso/) building stands on Plaza Sotomayor in the heart of the port city. It is interesting as part of an architectural ensemble associated with Chile's maritime history. That is how the building features in sightseeing itineraries: visitors see its façade and surrounding square before exploring the city's hills and neighborhoods.

Ada Tours includes this stop on the [Valparaíso, Viña del Mar and Pablo Neruda's House excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/). This is **a full-day trip from Santiago**, not a separate tour of the naval administration's working offices.

## What the itinerary confirms

First, travelers follow the road to the coast through Curacaví and Casablanca valleys. They then discover historic [Valparaíso](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). The named stops include Plaza Sotomayor and the historic Navy Headquarters, the Gervasoni and Atkinson promenades, Cerro Concepción and harbor views.

After the Valparaíso walking section, the itinerary continues to Viña del Mar, including the Flower Clock, Reñaca Beach, the seafront and Fonck Museum. Pablo Neruda's La Sebastiana house is mentioned as well. This format suits travelers who want to see both the historic and resort sides of Chile's coast in one day.

**Access to the interior of the Navy Headquarters is not confirmed in the itinerary.** Our route allows travelers to view the building from the square. A specialist visit to administrative offices or restricted areas cannot be promised on the basis of an ordinary city walk.

## Why Plaza Sotomayor matters

The square helps tell the maritime history of Valparaíso. Administrative architecture stands alongside port life, monuments and public spaces. International recognition of the city's historic quarter reflects the heritage of maritime trade and urban development on difficult terrain.

According to UNESCO, Valparaíso's historic quarter was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2003. Its significance includes port infrastructure, public spaces and historic funiculars on the slopes. **The UNESCO designation applies to the historic urban area**; it does not mean that every building has a separate listing.

Seeing the Headquarters from the square works well at the beginning of the walking section. Visitors first encounter the formal architecture of the lower city, then move to narrow streets, brightly painted houses and viewpoints on the hills.

## Combining the Headquarters, Paseo Atkinson and Viña del Mar

| Stage | What you see |
|---|---|
| Plaza Sotomayor | Architecture and port history |
| [Paseo Atkinson](/chile/place/paseo-atkinson/) | Walk and views from the hill |
| Viña del Mar | Promenade, beach and garden city |

From Plaza Sotomayor, the sightseeing route naturally continues toward Cerro Concepción. [Paseo Atkinson](/chile/place/paseo-atkinson/) has a different atmosphere, with small houses, lampposts, stairs and open views. This contrast explains why Valparaíso is known as a port built on hills.

If you want to focus solely on historic architecture, a full day incorporating Viña del Mar may feel busy. In-depth museum visits and leisurely walks require a separate allocation of time. The itinerary includes this attraction but does not specify the duration of every stop.

## Practical questions before choosing the excursion

The [current excursion from Santiago](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/) is described as **a full-day** program. The road journey to the coast is estimated at about 120 km and 1.5 hours, although traffic can affect actual timings.

Choose footwear suitable for Valparaíso's stairs and cobbled streets. A windbreaker is useful near the ocean. If entering museums is essential, ask whether admission is included in the quotation. For this excursion, the list of included tickets and a fixed price require separate confirmation.

## Frequently asked questions about Navy Headquarters excursions

### Can I see the Headquarters on a day trip from Santiago?

Yes. We show the building on the [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar sightseeing excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/) as an architectural stop at Plaza Sotomayor.

### Can visitors go inside?

The current itinerary does not confirm an interior visit. The excursion introduces the historic building from the square.

### How long does the excursion last?

It is a full-day program including Valparaíso, Viña del Mar and related coastal stops.

### Why is Valparaíso's historic center famous?

It is UNESCO-listed for its distinctive port architecture, public spaces and hillside development. The Navy Headquarters forms part of the surrounding historic ensemble.

### What comes after Plaza Sotomayor?

The route continues through the city's walking areas, including [Paseo Atkinson](/chile/place/paseo-atkinson/), before traveling onward to Viña del Mar.
